topic: squared vs cubed units — measurement error analysis

traps.desc: found the perimeter (added the sides) instead of the area
counted the cubes in one layer only

problems.desc: Correct unit for the classroom floor: square meters (m^2), because a floor is a flat surface covered by unit squares.
Correct unit for the juice in a glass: milliliters or cubic centimeters (cm^3), because juice fills space, so it is measured with unit cubes.
Correct unit for the length of a pencil: centimeters (cm), because length runs along one dimension only.

traps.desc: multiplied only two dimensions (found the area of the base)

problems.desc: Student names the error: Tomas's NUMBER (36) is right but his UNIT is wrong — volume is measured in cubic centimeters (cm^3), not square centimeters (cm^2), because it counts unit cubes filling the box, not unit squares covering a surface.

traps.desc: added the three dimensions instead of multiplying them

problems.desc: Student names the error: Lena multiplied by 100 only ONCE. A square meter is 100 cm by 100 cm, so each square meter holds 100 x 100 = 10000 square centimeters — squared units need the conversion factor twice.

traps.desc: used the length conversion factor only once
multiplied the edge by 3 instead of using it as a factor three times

problems.desc: Student names the error in Roy's claim: doubling the edge does not double the volume — the edge is a factor THREE times, so the volume is multiplied by 2 x 2 x 2 = 8. Accept any wording that says each of the three dimensions doubled.
